easy.def: A small fight over a little thing.
examples: They had a squabble.
The squabble was silly.
The kids had a squabble over a toy.

more.def: A noisy argument about something small.
examples: A squabble between the two brothers was over who sat by the window.
The squabble ended quickly.
A squabble broke out over who was first.

easy.def: To argue about a small thing.
examples: The kids squabble.
They squabbled over a toy.
Do not squabble.

more.def: To argue noisily about something that is not important.
examples: The birds squabbled over the crumbs.
The two sisters squabbled over a toy.
Do not squabble about who goes first.

easy.def: A small team.
examples: The squad practiced.
The soccer squad won.
A squad of firefighters came.

more.def: A small group of people who work or play together as a team.
examples: The cheerleading squad performed at the game.
A squad of firefighters rushed to the station.
Our soccer squad practices after school.

easy.def: A group of planes, ships or soldiers.
examples: A squadron of planes flew.
The squadron has ten ships.
The squadron marched.

more.def: A group of airplanes, ships or soldiers that work together.
examples: A squadron of planes flew over the stadium.
The squadron of ships sailed out of the harbor.
Each squadron had its own flag.

easy.def: A short, strong burst of wind and rain.
examples: A squall came up.
The squall was fast.
The squall hit the boat.

more.def: A sudden, strong wind that often brings rain or snow and soon passes.
examples: A squall tossed the little boat on the waves.
The picnic was ruined by a sudden squall.
Dark clouds brought a squall that was over in minutes.

easy.def: To waste money or time.
examples: Do not squander your money.
He squandered his chance.
She squandered the day.

more.def: To waste something, such as money or time, in a foolish way.
examples: Do not squander your allowance on candy.
He squandered the whole afternoon.
They squandered their chance to win.

easy.def: A shape with four equal sides.
examples: Draw a square.
A square has four sides.
The box is a square.

more.def: A flat shape with four straight sides that are all the same length.
examples: Draw a square with a ruler.
A chessboard has sixty-four squares.
The picture was cut into a square.

easy.def: Shaped like a square.
examples: The table is square.
A square window.
The box is square.

more.def: Having four equal sides and four right angles.
examples: The garden bed is square.
A square window lets in light.
We sat around the square table.

easy.def: An open area in a town.
examples: We met in the square.
The town square.
Pigeons live in the square.

more.def: An open area in a town or city with buildings around it.
examples: The market is held in the town square.
Pigeons gathered in the square.
People met in the square for the parade.

easy.def: To crush flat.
examples: I squash the box.
She squashed the bug.
The cat squashed the pillow.

more.def: To press something until it is flat or out of shape.
examples: I squashed the empty box flat.
She accidentally squashed the bread.
The suitcase was squashed under the bags.

easy.def: A hard-skinned vegetable.
examples: I ate squash.
The squash is orange.
Squash grows on a vine.

more.def: A vegetable with a thick skin and soft flesh, such as a pumpkin or zucchini.
examples: Mom baked butternut squash for dinner.
The squash is orange inside.
She roasted the squash with butter.

easy.def: Soft and easy to squeeze.
examples: The pillow is squashy.
A squashy ball.
The squashy sofa.

more.def: Soft, wet or easy to squeeze flat.
examples: The squashy cushion sank under her weight.
The squashy mud squelched under our boots.
He gave the squashy ball a squeeze.

easy.def: To bend your knees and lower your body close to the ground.
examples: I squat to tie my shoe.
She squatted by the pond.
We squat to look at the bug.

more.def: To crouch down low with your knees bent.
examples: I squatted down to look at the ant.
She squatted by the pond and watched the tadpoles.
The children squatted in a circle around the campfire.

easy.def: Short and thick.
examples: The squat house was made of stone.
A squat jar sat on the shelf.
The squat tower was round.

more.def: Short and wide, in a way that seems heavy.
examples: A squat stone house sat at the end of the lane.
The squat jar held the cookie dough.
The tree was short and squat, with thick branches.

easy.def: To make a loud, rough cry, like a bird.
examples: The parrot squawks.
A seagull squawked.
The crows squawk.

more.def: To make a loud, harsh cry, as some birds do.
examples: The parrot squawked loudly when we walked in.
A seagull squawked and stole a chip from my plate.
The crows squawked in the tall trees at dawn.

easy.def: A loud, rough cry made by a bird.
examples: I heard a squawk.
The parrot let out a squawk.
A squawk came from the tree.

more.def: A loud, harsh cry, especially from a bird.
examples: I heard a loud squawk from the parrot.
A squawk came from the tree as the crow flew away.
The seagull let out a squawk when it saw the food.

easy.def: To make a short, high sound.
examples: The mouse squeaks.
The door squeaked.
The shoes squeak.

more.def: To make a short, high, thin sound.
examples: The mouse squeaked in the corner.
The door squeaked on its hinges.
My new shoes squeak.

easy.def: Making a high, small sound.
examples: The door is squeaky.
A squeaky toy.
A squeaky voice.

more.def: Making a high, thin sound like a mouse or a rusty hinge.
examples: The squeaky door needs some oil.
The puppy chewed its squeaky toy.
The mouse made a squeaky noise as it ran under the stove.

easy.def: To make a long, high sound.
examples: The pig squealed.
The brakes squeal.
The kids squealed with joy.

more.def: To make a long, high, sharp sound.
examples: The pig squealed when it saw its food.
The brakes squealed as the bus stopped.
The kids squealed with joy on the slide.

easy.def: Easily upset by yucky things.
examples: I am squeamish about bugs.
She is squeamish.
He felt squeamish.

more.def: Easily made to feel sick or upset by things that are gross.
examples: I am squeamish about touching worms.
She felt squeamish when she saw the mess.
He is squeamish at the sight of a shot.

easy.def: To press something hard from all sides.
examples: I squeeze the sponge.
She squeezed the lemon.
He squeezed my hand.

more.def: To press something firmly from the sides, often to get liquid out or to fit into a small space.
examples: She squeezed a lemon to make lemonade.
The cat squeezed through the small hole.
He squeezed my hand to say goodbye.

easy.def: To make a wet, sucking sound.
examples: My boots squelch in the mud.
The mud squelched.
He squelched across the field.

more.def: To make a wet, sucking sound, like walking through thick mud.
examples: My boots squelched in the mud.
The wet sponge squelched when I squeezed it.
He squelched across the wet field.

easy.def: A sea animal with a long body and ten arms.
examples: A squid swam by.
The squid has long arms.
We saw a squid at the aquarium.

more.def: A sea animal with a soft body and ten long arms that can squirt dark ink to escape from danger.
examples: A squid shot out a cloud of dark ink and darted away from the fish.
The giant squid lives deep in the ocean.
Squid swim by pushing water out of their bodies.

easy.def: A little wavy line.
examples: I drew a squiggle.
A squiggle on the page.
The squiggle is red.

more.def: A short, wavy or curly line that is drawn or written.
examples: I drew a squiggle on the paper and turned it into a snake.
His handwriting looked like a row of squiggles.
The squiggles on the screen showed the sound waves.

easy.def: Wavy and twisty.
examples: A squiggly line.
The squiggly worm.
A squiggly drawing.

more.def: Wavy, curly and twisting.
examples: He drew a squiggly line across the page.
A squiggly worm wriggled on the path.
The squiggly pattern looked like a snake.

easy.def: To look with your eyes almost shut.
examples: I squint in the sun.
He squinted at the sign.
She squinted at the bright light.

more.def: To look at something with your eyes partly closed, to see better or to keep out light.
examples: I squinted because the sun was so bright.
He squinted to read the tiny words on the sign.
The hikers squinted at the far-off mountain.

easy.def: A look with your eyes almost shut.
examples: He gave a squint at the sun.
She had a squint in the sun.
There was a squint on his face.

more.def: A look with the eyes partly closed.
examples: He gave a squint at the bright sky.
She looked at the far-off sign with a squint.
His squint showed that the light was too bright.

easy.def: A young man who helped a knight long ago.
examples: The squire carried the shield.
A squire helped the knight.
The squire was young.

more.def: A young man who served and helped a knight in the time of castles.
examples: The squire carried the knight's shield.
A squire polished the knight's armor.
The young squire dreamed of becoming a knight.

easy.def: To wiggle and twist your body.
examples: The baby squirmed.
I squirmed in my seat.
The worm squirms.

more.def: To wiggle and twist your body, because you are uncomfortable or are trying to get away.
examples: The baby squirmed in my arms and wanted to get down.
I squirmed in my seat during the long speech.
The worm squirmed on the hook.

easy.def: A small animal with a bushy tail that climbs trees.
examples: The squirrel ate a nut.
A squirrel ran up the tree.
The squirrel has a bushy tail.

more.def: A small furry animal with a bushy tail that lives in trees and eats nuts.
examples: The squirrel buried an acorn in the lawn.
A squirrel scampered up the oak.
Squirrels gather nuts in the fall.

easy.def: To shoot out a thin stream of liquid.
examples: I squirt the water.
The hose squirted.
He squirted lemon.

more.def: To send out liquid in a thin, fast stream.
examples: I squirted water from the hose.
The orange squirted juice in my eye.
She squirted ketchup on her fries.

easy.def: To squeeze something soft.
examples: I squished the clay.
The mud squished.
Don't squish the bread.

more.def: To crush or squeeze something soft so that it gets flat, or to make a soft, wet sound.
examples: I squished the clay between my fingers.
The mud squished under my boots as I walked.
Don't squish the bread in the bottom of the bag.

easy.def: Soft and wet.
examples: The mud is squishy.
A squishy toy.
The squishy peach.

more.def: Soft and wet so that it squashes when you press it.
examples: The mud was squishy under my boots.
I squeezed the squishy toy.
The ripe peach was squishy.
